title: Cyber insurance for companies: preparing a risk file

seo.description: Prepare a company cyber risk file covering digital operations, access, backups, recovery costs and the conditions of a potential insurance proposal.

author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
Cyber insurance for a company must be considered against its actual systems, data and operations. A product name does not confirm payment for every loss following a computer attack. For a business in the Republic of Moldova, the first step is a risk file: what could be affected, how it is protected and what restarting operations would cost.

This article helps management, the person responsible for IT and the broker prepare their discussion. It is information, not confirmation that a particular cyber product is available for your company. Eligibility, the insurer, conditions and included services must be checked separately. Do not send passwords, access keys or copies of customer databases with an initial assessment request.

Start with operations that depend on digital systems

List the activities you cannot continue without applications or connectivity: receiving orders, recording stock, issuing invoices, scheduling transport or providing customer services. For each activity, identify the application and responsible person. A computer inventory alone does not explain how dependent the company is on a system.

Distinguish an inconvenient interruption from one that stops deliveries. Where a temporary manual procedure exists, describe it realistically: who can use it, for how long and with what limitations. An IT maintenance agreement does not by itself demonstrate that the entire business is protected.

Describe data without copying it into the file

Identify the categories of information processed, such as contact details, commercial documents, employee information or technical files. State where they are stored and who manages them. An initial assessment needs categories and an approximate scale of activity, not files containing customers' personal data.

Include information received from partners and data held by a supplier on the company's behalf. An accountant, an online shop and a transport business may have very different dependencies. Legal requirements concerning data must be reviewed separately with the appropriate specialist. A policy is not a substitute for that review.

Draw a simple supplier map

Record who hosts applications, administers email and provides technical support. Show which services operate on the premises and which are supplied externally. There is no need to publish sensitive technical addresses or details that would enable access to the company's systems.

For each important supplier, keep the contract, contact person and explanation of the incident procedure. Check whether data can be recovered and the supplier replaced during an interruption. Hosting in the cloud does not itself establish an independent backup, rapid recovery or insurance coverage.

Describe access controls as they actually operate

Prepare an explanation of administrator accounts, remote access and multi-factor authentication. The latter means checking identity using more than a password. State which services have it enabled and where exceptions remain, without disclosing authentication codes or recovery methods.

Explain how accounts are closed when people leave and how a new colleague's permissions are approved. If a control is only planned, identify it as planned. An optimistic questionnaire answer can conceal exactly the issue that needs discussing before a potential proposal is assessed.

Check restoration, not just the existence of backups

A backup is a copy of data kept for recovery. Describe what is saved, how often and who can start restoration. Record the date of a real test and what was successfully recovered. An automatic message saying copying finished does not mean the entire business can resume.

Ask the technical team about separating backups from working systems and accessing them during an incident. Describe the documents needed for recovery as well. These are preparation questions, not universal technical instructions or evidence that a particular insurer's conditions have been satisfied.

Separate equipment damage from a cyber incident

A physically damaged server, data encrypted by an attacker and a payment sent to the wrong account are different situations. Describe them separately when asking about possible insurance solutions. Insuring laptops does not automatically include data loss, email fraud or interruption of digital services.

Similarly, a possible cyber policy should not be assumed to replace all physical property. Ask for the boundaries between equipment, information, the company's own costs and other people's claims. The IT equipment article complements this assessment but does not replace reading each contract's conditions.

Estimate expenditure by recovery stage

Build a working scenario without invented figures: detecting the incident, isolating the problem, checking data, restoring systems and returning to normal operations. Ask the IT team to identify potentially necessary external services. Management can then estimate costs using contracts, received rates and the company's own records.

Separate additional expenditure from income that is delayed or lost. Avoid counting the same loss in two categories. The resulting document is an internal discussion estimate, not the amount an insurer would pay. The contractual method of assessing a loss requires a separate check.

Review fraud and money transfers separately

Prepare questions about an employee receiving an altered invoice or a message apparently sent by a director. Ask whether such events are included, excluded or assessed under another product category. The word “fraud” in a commercial presentation is not a sufficient answer.

Describe how the company checks changes to a supplier's bank account and approves payments. Do not enter partners' actual bank details into public forms. If a suspicious transaction has already occurred, follow the incident procedure and contact the relevant institutions. A new policy must not be presented as a solution to a known event.

Prepare an incident response list

Decide who coordinates internally, who contacts suppliers and who records decisions. The list should remain available when company email is not working. Keep a version accessible to authorised people without embedding passwords or technical keys in the document.

During an incident, protecting people and limiting consequences come first. Preserve relevant information and obtain specialist help before operations that could destroy evidence. If an insurance contract exists, check its contacts, notification procedure and approval of services. Do not invent a single deadline applicable to every policy.

Compare proposals through written questions

Request the same information for each option: the insured entity, systems and activities assessed, events, limits and exclusions. Exclusions are situations for which the contract provides no cover. An excess or deductible is the part of a loss borne by the insured under the contract. Request calculation examples for the actual proposal, not unrelated illustrations.

Ask separately about external suppliers, territories, approved expenditure and circumstances already known. Mark answers that remain unconfirmed. A short list of open points is more useful than “complete protection”, which does not explain what happens during a real incident.

An example for a company operating from several locations

Imagine a business with an administrative office in Chișinău and two distribution points. Orders are managed in a shared application, while stock is confirmed at each location. The risk file explains dependence on the application, its supplier and the temporary delivery procedure without online access.

The finance officer separately estimates recovery expenditure and the IT administrator documents a restoration test. This is a hypothetical organisational example, not an ING Broker customer or a paid claim. It shows which information makes a discussion more precise without promising an insurance outcome.

Keep a register of decisions and unresolved points

For each assessment question, record the answer, supporting document and person able to confirm it. The IT lead might show restoration results, while management confirms operational priorities. Do not ask one person to certify technical, legal and financial matters they do not directly understand.

Before renewal, review changes such as new applications, premises, suppliers, business acquisitions or remote access arrangements. Keep unanswered questions with an owner responsible for clarification. The file should describe the current position, not an old configuration copied for convenience. This organisation assists proposal checking but does not replace technical control or the insurer's acceptance.

Information to prepare for the first discussion

  • Company activities, locations and applications on which operations depend.
  • Data categories and suppliers hosting or administering them.
  • Access controls and the date of the latest recovery test.
  • An incident history described factually without public disclosure of sensitive details.
  • An interruption scenario and an internal expenditure estimate.

Frequently asked questions about cyber assessment

How much does cyber insurance cost for a company in Moldova?

This article provides no verified tariff for your business. Price can be discussed only after an eligible solution and its proposed conditions are confirmed. Prepare details of activities, systems, security controls and requested limits. Do not compare the payment alone while ignoring exclusions and costs retained by the company.

Is antivirus software enough for the risk assessment?

A program name does not describe the whole protection arrangement. The file should also explain access, backups, suppliers, updates and response organisation. IT specialists perform technical checks, while the insurer decides risk acceptance and contractual conditions.

Should passwords or customer data be sent?

No. Initially, describe data categories and processes. Any sensitive document needed later should be sent only through an authorised channel and within the necessary scope. A broker does not need your password to discuss how a risk file should be organised.

Does this article confirm that ING Broker offers every cyber policy?

No. It explains preparation for a company assessment in Moldova. Availability, conditions and the possibility of brokering a particular solution require separate confirmation. A photograph or recommendation list is neither an offer nor confirmation of compensation.
